rules.note: Sharpens RULE-COUNSEL-057 rather than qualifying it — found by the peer session via direct ÖSYM domain fetch plus convergent independent YKS-calculator cross-check, reported to and incorporated by this session.

rules.statement: Canada's named 'holistic supplementary application' competitive programs are not one uniform mechanism: Waterloo Engineering's AIF explicitly invites activity/accomplishment description, while Queen's Commerce and McMaster Health Sciences score written/video responses to structured reflective prompts with no activities-list criterion in their own published rubrics. Never assume 'holistic supplementary application' means the same evaluation mechanism across different named programs without checking each program's own rubric.

For a Queen's-Commerce- or McMaster-HHSP-track student specifically, never phrase supplementary-application advice as 'add more activities to your profile' — by these programs' own published rubrics, the scored lever is reflective-response quality on specific prompts, not activity-list breadth.
rules.note: Direct consequence of RULE-COUNSEL-110's primary-source finding.

rules.statement: This package's earlier characterization of the University of Toronto as running an explicitly holistic process weighing leadership/community involvement/extracurricular activities for its general admissions process is not confirmed by UofT's own official assessment page, which instead describes a grade/prerequisite-driven general process with program-specific (not universal) supplemental requirements. The original claim is withdrawn for UofT's general process, not merely qualified.
rules.note: A primary-source check that corrected rather than merely sharpened a prior medium-confidence secondary claim — see RULE-COUNSEL-107 for the same discipline applied previously to a social-work claim.

rules.statement: For a UK-track target, weight subject-relevant intellectual_curiosity/research/execution_project_depth/awards_distinction high and their non-subject-relevant counterparts low; weight leadership low-medium regardless of subject-relevance; weight community_impact low except for medicine.
rules.note: Directionally sourced via RULE-COUNSEL-058 (official UCAS guidance); the specific per-dimension ordinal calls are this document's own reasoned extension, not independently verified dimension-by-dimension against UCAS guidance.

rules.statement: For a France/Parcoursup-track target: academics maps to the 'Résultats académiques'/'Compétences académiques' champs (high-weighted); intellectual_curiosity maps to 'Savoir-être' (curiosité intellectuelle, ouverture au monde) and subject-specific 'Motivation'; leadership/community_impact map to the 'Engagements, activités' champ (school-council engagement, civic service named explicitly). All 5 champs are mandatorily percentage-weighted per formation summing to 100%, but any single formation's exact percentage per champ is formation-specific, not general knowledge.
rules.note: Originally marked fully unresolved (no per-dimension sourcing); substantially resolved on a follow-up pass after directly reading DGESIP's official CGEV framework document. See RULE-COUNSEL-117 for the underlying source finding.

rules.statement: Tier alone is insufficient for Tier-3-with-named-carve-out targets; ORYN's counselor must know the specific named program and what that program's own rubric scores before recommending anything, since carve-out mechanisms range from activity-description to pure reflective-response scoring to skills auditions to standardized aptitude tests.
rules.note: Direct consequence of RULE-COUNSEL-110's primary-source finding.

rules.statement: Country/tier-level conditioning and field-level (major-family) conditioning must compose together; medicine alone demonstrates the 'exception direction' flips by country (activity-rewarding in US/UK, aptitude-test-gated in Switzerland, more-exam-dominated-than-usual in Turkey), so neither level of conditioning is sufficient alone.
rules.note: High confidence for the medicine cases specifically (each individually sourced elsewhere in this package: RULE-COUNSEL-032/033/058/065/057/103); medium for how broadly this generalizes to fields beyond medicine, which this document did not check.

rules.statement: France's Parcoursup applications are evaluated against exactly 5 nationally-defined evaluation fields (academic results, academic competencies/methodology, soft skills, motivation/program-fit, activities/engagement), each mandatorily assigned a formation-specific percentage weight summing to 100%, per DGESIP's official CGEV framework document. Confirms activities/engagement is a real, structurally-guaranteed evaluation category, not optional or vague.
rules.note: Official DGESIP document, directly extracted via pypdf after WebFetch's own extractor failed on this file.

rules.statement: ORYN's recommendation vocabulary has no category for 'practice articulating existing experience in a specific structured format' (e.g. rehearsing a reflective response to Queen's-Commerce-style prompts), as distinct from 'go get more/better experience' -- the entire achievement-tier evidence model is built around logged achievements, not response-rehearsal preparation.
rules.note: A real gap this persona's own walkthrough demonstrates the current model cannot cleanly express, not a hypothetical concern.

rules.statement: Per-target explanations for a shared recommended action must name the mechanism by which each target values it (direct scored evidence vs. indirect raw material for a differently-scored assessment), not only the framing register -- a blended or mechanism-silent explanation risks a student over-investing in the wrong kind of preparation for at least one target, even when the recommended action is correctly the same for both.
rules.note: Direct consequence of Persona J's walkthrough; sharpens RULE-COUNSEL-066 rather than replacing it.

rules.statement: ORYN's evidence/recommendation model needs to distinguish at least three structurally different non-academic assessment types: achievement-evidence-based (US/UK/Waterloo), institution-authored reflective response (Queen's Commerce/McMaster HHSP), and standardized third-party situational-judgment testing (CASPer -- 500+ programs, medicine/health-sciences/PA/nursing/dental-hygiene currently, expanding into education/business/engineering). Each needs different preparation guidance.
rules.note: Found by checking whether Persona J's gap (RULE-COUNSEL-118) generalizes beyond Queen's/McMaster specifically -- it does, and further than expected.

rules.statement: UK medicine/dentistry admission is a compound case, not just grades plus holistic clinical-exposure evidence: 57 UK universities also require the UCAT, which includes a separately-banded Situational Judgement Test subtest -- not activity-based at all. Confirms RULE-COUNSEL-120's 'standardized third-party situational-judgment testing' category generalizes beyond CASPer/North America as a recurring structural type (different specific instruments per region), not a single tool.
rules.note: Checked directly after RULE-COUNSEL-120 raised the question of how far the typology generalizes; UCAT confirms it's a real category, not a CASPer-specific quirk.

rules.statement: Ireland's CAO system is Tier 3 (Leaving Certificate points, no general activity weight, confirmed via CAO's own official page) with medicine as a named exception in the aptitude-test direction (HPAT, a 117-question multiple-choice test including a 40%-weighted 'Understanding People' interpersonal-judgment section) -- the same structural pattern as the UK's UCAT, a second country confirming RULE-COUNSEL-121 generalizes.
rules.note: Extends the generic-Europe-fallback sample from 7 to 8 countries (see RULE-COUNSEL-075's updated count) and finds a second UCAT-shaped medicine exception, suggesting this may be a recurring pattern worth checking whenever a new country is researched.

rules.statement: DECA's own official competitive-events page names specific, distinct entrepreneurship events (Start-Up Business Plan, Independent Business Plan, Franchise Business Plan, International Business Plan, Innovation Plan, Entrepreneurship Series) rather than one generic 'business competition' -- gives Pathway 2 the same named-program evidence-tier hook Pathways 1 and 3 already had.

Derive an approximate developmental stage (yearsUntilGraduation = graduation_year - currentYear) from data ORYN already collects; expose it as a non-binding display default a student can override, never as a hard eligibility gate or a claim of precision it doesn't have. Degrade to 'insufficient data for timing context' for education_stage='other' or curriculum='other' rather than silently defaulting to one country's grade system.

Stage (years until graduation) determines WHAT KIND of recommendation is appropriate; the student's own time budget determines HOW MUCH/HOW BIG. Never let a tight time budget silently substitute a breadth-type recommendation for a depth-type one -- if nothing depth-appropriate fits, say so explicitly rather than swapping category.

A student outside the typical phase pattern for their stage is not automatically a gap. Distinguish objective time-remaining from implied deficiency: a Phase-1 student with genuine early depth should not be pushed toward artificial breadth; a Phase-2 student who is broad due to a recent, legitimate interest shift should have that context surfaced, not be penalized as if the shift never happened.

Treat 'Computer Science' as an umbrella, not a single skill -- competitive-programming-style algorithmic problem-solving and building/shipping user-facing products are both legitimately 'CS' but develop measurably different things.

When counseling a CS-interested student, distinguish at minimum three evidence types -- sustained independent build (execution_project_depth), algorithmic competition (quantitative/algorithmic reasoning under contest conditions), and time-boxed hackathon/team build (rapid-build + teamwork) -- rather than treating 'did something CS-related' as one undifferentiated signal.

'I like math' may mean enjoying proof/abstraction (pure track), applied problem-solving with formulas (applied track), or analyzing data (statistics track) -- these predict different downstream fits and should not be treated as one undifferentiated signal.

A stated interest in 'physics' or 'chemistry' should be probed for which pole a student actually enjoys -- theoretical/mathematical problem-solving vs. hands-on experimental work reward different exploration experiences.
'Biology' spans wet-lab/bench work, field/ecological work, and computational biology -- probing which a student means matters as much here as for computing/mathematics.

A biology major is necessary for essentially no clinical health profession in most systems -- pre-med 'requirements' are typically specific courses, not a mandated major. Must be stated explicitly to counteract a common real-world misconception.

'Engineering' as a stated interest is at least as broad as 'Computer Science' or 'Biology' -- a student should sample more than one of mechanical/civil/aerospace/electrical before narrowing, since they involve meaningfully different day-to-day work despite a shared first-year curriculum.

PE-equivalent licensure necessity varies substantially by role AND industry, not just by engineering subfield -- civil engineers stamping public infrastructure plans are the clearest necessity case; many ME/EE/AE industry roles (esp. aerospace/defense, tech-adjacent EE) practice career-long without one. A specific student's situation should be checked against target industry/employer expectations, not inferred from subfield alone.

Biomedical engineering is not a subset of 'pre-med' and should not be counseled as one -- it is an engineering discipline whose graduates mostly go into engineering/industry/research roles, not clinical practice. A student wanting to become a physician does not need a biomedical engineering degree. (Generalizes RULE-COUNSEL-208 to this field.)

Economics is a genuinely quantitative social science -- a student drawn to it purely for real-world relevance (news/policy) without appetite for the underlying statistics/econometrics is a real, worth-surfacing mismatch signal (a counseling conversation topic, not a disqualification).

Entrepreneurship is about originating and testing a new venture; general business/management study is about operating and improving an existing one. A strong management-track profile is not automatically evidence of entrepreneurial capability, and vice versa.

DECA competitive events split into three genuinely different types: role-play/case-study and online simulations (applied business-scenario reasoning under simulated conditions -- not entrepreneurship evidence, since no real venture is originated/tested) vs. Business Operations Research Events (original research on an annually-changing topic, individually or in teams of up to three -- structurally closer to the research dimension than to a business simulation). Evaluate DECA involvement by which event type a student actually did.
rules.note: Refined after locating DECA's own official event-type breakdown (deca.org/compete) -- the original version treated DECA as one undifferentiated event type.

rules.statement: 'Environmental science' and 'sustainability' are not the same activity profile -- a student drawn to fieldwork/conservation and one drawn to sustainability policy/business practice are both legitimately in this family but benefit from different exploration experiences.

Never state a probability of admission/success/outcome without a validated statistical model backing it -- restates the founder spec's non-negotiable #5 as an explainability rule for why[]/warnings[] text specifically.

Never let a ProfileGap (Oryn's own developmental judgment) imply a university 'requires' addressing it -- only a sourced, per-university RequirementEvaluationSummary is allowed to make a requirement-style claim.

Never hide low confidence behind confident-sounding language -- a confidence:'low' recommendation must lead with the data gap itself, not bury it in a trailing warning the student might not read as carefully.

Distinguish 'verified information' from 'Oryn analysis' in the actual RENDERED text a student sees, not just internally in the data model -- externally-sourced content (a requirement's own reasoning) should be visually/textually distinguishable from Oryn's own developmental judgment.

A deprioritize/avoid_for_now recommendation's why[] must always include a redirect -- either the specific higher-value gap it's implicitly weighed against, or an honest statement that it's simply not currently a priority given time constraints -- never a bare 'this is low value' with no comparison point.

Every piece of reasoning this research package contributes must enter why[]/warnings[] as a parameterized template string keyed to a real structured fact -- never as a place where an LLM is asked to 'explain this in your own words' for the deterministic pipeline. Richer nuance that doesn't fit a short template belongs in the optional LLM narration layer's input context, still wrapped in the existing untrusted-data boundary -- never a relaxation of the deterministic pipeline's no-free-text rule.

Never present a specific named opportunity/program sourced only from secondary/aggregator discovery as a confirmed, current, verified offering to a student -- it must first pass through ORYN's actual opportunity-acquisition/verification pipeline. This research package documents pathway TYPES, not a verified directory.
rules.note: The peer branch independently minted a DIFFERENT RULE-COUNSEL-222 (a redundancy/timing-composition fix, in their 09-persona-testing.md) -- flagged, not resolved. See docs/handoffs/research-counseling-intelligence.md.

rules.statement: Never infer a student's aptitude, interest, or fit for any field from a demographic attribute (nationality, gender, school type, socioeconomic signal, or any similar proxy).
rules.note: Directly restates the mission brief's own explicit 'what Oryn must not do' list verbatim; minted here because neither branch had numbered it explicitly yet, though both branches' actual document content is already consistent with it throughout.

rules.statement: Never present one career family as objectively 'better' than another (e.g., by salary or prestige) independent of the specific student's own stated interests/goals.

Never equate a career family's aggregate popularity or labor-market growth rate with a claim about a specific student's likely fit or success in it -- every BLS growth statistic cited across this package's family docs is an aggregate US labor-market data point, never a claim about an individual student's prospects.

Where a UK-facing student needs career-outlook grounding, prefer National Careers Service job profiles over BLS/O*NET -- they are the UK's own official equivalent, not a secondary source, and salary/qualification framing does not transfer across countries even when the occupation name is identical.

Turkey's TMMOB chamber-registration/title-protection system is structurally distinct from BOTH the US PE system (voluntary-until-triggered-by-specific-practice) and the UK CEng system (institution-administered chartered status layered on top of an unrestricted base right to practice) -- a Turkey-target engineering student should not have US/UK licensure framing applied to them by default.

Never apply US-holistic-admissions-derived reasoning (depth-over-breadth, extracurricular signaling, redundancy/saturation logic) with the same directness to a student targeting an admissions system with a fundamentally different structure -- e.g. Turkey's exam-score-dominated YKS placement (where academics is doing nearly all the admissions work and the other 8 ProfileDimensions matter for real development but should not be framed as admissions-relevant), or the UK's UCAS system (which weights subject-relevant super-curricular engagement over general extracurricular breadth more heavily than US holistic review does). Oryn's developmental framing remains valid regardless of geography; its ADMISSIONS-RELEVANCE framing must be geography-conditional. Assessed as the single highest-leverage open item this whole research package surfaced (verified independently by both sessions).
rules.note: Originally surfaced by the peer session's persona-testing pass, independently verified by this session via direct ÖSYM/YKS and UCAS sourcing. Highest-priority item for any future continuation of this research.

rules.statement: Unlike DECA/FBLA-style simulated-scenario competitions (RULE-COUNSEL-214), UK's Young Enterprise Company Programme genuinely clears the 'real, tested venture' bar for entrepreneurship evidence -- real company, real bank account, real customers, not a simulation. A UK student's participation should be evaluated against the founder spec's 'idea -> built -> tested' ladder, not treated as equivalent to a DECA/FBLA placement.

Absent a specific target-university signal, a target_geography='turkey' student should be treated as PROBABLY YKS-track by default for the purposes of RULE-COUNSEL-228 (not framing Oryn's developmental dimensions as admissions-relevant) -- not because every Turkey-targeting student is YKS-track (some target private/foundation universities with their own supplementary admissions criteria, or study abroad), but because YKS-track public-university placement is the larger, more common case, and wrongly suppressing US-holistic-style framing for a private/abroad-track student is a much less harmful failure mode than the reverse. Revisit the moment the student adds a specific target university whose actual admission model can be checked.
rules.note: Surfaced by this session's own persona-stress-test of RULE-COUNSEL-228 against a concrete hypothetical (14-year-old, Turkey, no target universities yet) -- found that the rule's own 'targeting Turkish public university placement specifically' condition has no way to be checked for a young student, and needed an explicit default.

rules.statement: The peer branch's 05-redundancy-saturation.md grounds its 'do not recommend more of an already-strong area' logic in two justifications: signal-quality-to-evaluators, and opportunity-cost-under-time-constraint. For a YKS-track student (RULE-COUNSEL-228/230), only the opportunity-cost justification remains valid -- there is no evaluator reading a holistic file in YKS placement, so the signal-quality justification asserts something false if included in an explanation shown to a YKS-track student. Construct avoid_for_now/redundancy explanations for YKS-track students from opportunity-cost alone.
rules.note: Found by checking RULE-COUNSEL-228's Turkey caveat directly against the peer branch's own redundancy-saturation document rather than leaving it as an unspecified general pointer.

rules.statement: 'Wanting to teach' is not one undifferentiated interest -- elementary generalist, secondary subject-specialist, and special education involve substantially different day-to-day work and, in most systems, different credentialing tracks.

Subject-matter achievement is not the same evidence as enjoying/being effective at teaching that subject -- sustained, structured tutoring or instruction of others is meaningfully stronger evidence for the education/teaching family than subject mastery alone.

Turkey's teaching-credential system is actively changing (MEB material indicates a new Milli Egitim Akademisi training requirement beyond KPSS) -- do not give a Turkey-target student a static one-time description of this pathway; re-verify against MEB's current guidance.
rules.note: Sourced from MEB's own regulation for the existing KPSS/pedagogical-formation structure (high confidence); the National Education Academy transition itself is secondary-reported, not yet fetched from MEB's own final rule text (medium confidence for that specific claim).

rules.statement: US, UK, and Turkey teaching credentialing all converge on the same two-part structure (a relevant degree plus a separate pedagogical/professional credentialing step) despite very different specific mechanics -- state this general pattern to students while being explicit the exact mechanics are country-specific and must not be conflated.

For a student with more than one active target geography carrying materially different admissions logic, never silently pick one target's admissions-relevance framing and present it as universally true -- either give a per-target breakdown of why a recommendation matters differently to each, or default to the most-specific/most-active target's framing (never a bare geography-average).
rules.note: Surfaced by the peer session's persona-testing pass (persona H: IB curriculum, mixed UK/Germany targets). An open product/UI design question, not fully resolved by this research -- which of the two options is better is flagged for open-questions tracking on both branches.

rules.statement: 'Music' or 'performing arts' spans meaningfully different day-to-day activities and, sometimes, genuinely different admission mechanisms (e.g. classical conservatory audition vs. general performing-arts degree) -- probe which a student means before treating it as one interest.

Turkish conservatory/performing-arts admission is NOT purely academic-exam-driven the way the general YKS system is (RULE-COUNSEL-228) -- it is a hybrid of a lower TYT score threshold plus a talent/audition exam, structurally closer to the UK's 'talent can substitute for credentials' pattern. Do not apply the blanket YKS caveat to a Turkey-target student interested specifically in this family without this refinement.
rules.note: Verified directly against official Turkish state-conservatory talent-exam guidance, not secondhand.

rules.statement: yearsUntilGraduation <= 0 is not one situation -- distinguish a genuine gap year (Phase 2 framing still applies, often more urgently), actual progression to undergraduate stage (a different product surface entirely, out of this package's scope), and stale profile data (a past-due graduation_year the student never updated) before recommending anything. Never collapse these into one generic 'graduated' treatment.
rules.note: Found on this session's own re-read of its own document, not from an external report -- the yearsUntilGraduation<=0 table row existed from the start but was never actually discussed.

rules.statement: Never assume performing-arts performance-track pathways (dance specifically, per BLS's own 'highest rates of injuries and illnesses' statement) are equally accessible to every student without a stated need -- and never assume the reverse, that a disability precludes this family (adaptive dance, wheelchair-inclusive performance, disability arts are real practice areas).
rules.note: Found on this session's own re-read, prompted by awareness of the peer's health/disability-access work in their gap-framework -- this document's own first draft said nothing about it despite a directly relevant, sourced BLS data point.

rules.statement: Germany's engineering credentialing is a fourth, genuinely distinct model from US/UK/Turkey: the 'Ingenieur' title is protected by state-level Ingenieurgesetz legislation, requiring completion of a foundational technical-engineering-scientific degree (bachelor's or master's) at a recognized German institution -- verified directly against VDI's own page: no separate engineering-chamber registration is required (unlike architecture's Architektenkammer, family 16, or Turkey's TMMOB), and the right to use the title, once earned in one state, applies across all 16 German states. Practice itself is NOT regulated -- unlike the US (practice-gated PE licensure for specific activities) and Turkey (chamber registration required to practice at all). VDI is the central professional association but is explicitly not a licensing body. Use this four-way comparison (US/UK/Turkey/Germany) as the canonical illustration of why licensure framing must be country-specific, never one global claim.
rules.note: Upgraded from medium-high (secondary sourcing) to high via direct fetch of VDI's own official page, corroborated by Bundesingenieurkammer's own page and Bavaria's own state statutory text -- mirrors the peer session's same-pattern upgrade for its own German professional-body sources (law/BRAK, psychology/BMG).

rules.statement: YKS placement score is not pure exam score -- it also folds in OBP (Ortaogretim Basari Puani, a school-achievement score derived from the student's diploma grade), applied at a small, capped coefficient (commonly described as ~0.12 of the placement formula, roughly a maximum of 60 points, halved to ~0.06 for a candidate previously placed in a program). This sharpens rather than weakens RULE-COUNSEL-228: the only non-exam-day channel reaching a YKS placement score is still purely grades-based (the academics dimension, via diploma grade), capped small, and structurally distinct from anything an extracurricular activity, award, or leadership role could contribute. There remains no channel by which leadership, community_impact, entrepreneurship, research, or awards_distinction evidence reaches YKS placement.
rules.note: Existence and rough size of the OBP channel: high confidence (direct osym.gov.tr fetch confirmed ÖSYM publishes exact coefficient tables as standing practice). Exact current-year ~0.12/~0.06 coefficient values: medium confidence (convergent multi-source secondary corroboration, not independently re-derived from ÖSYM's own current-year table this pass).

rules.statement: Do not assume the Casper situational-judgment test (or a Casper-style assessment) applies to a US-target teaching-track student by default. Casper is confirmed used for admission INTO teacher-education programs (a different gate from post-degree licensure) at multiple Canadian/Australian institutions (Vancouver Island University, Monash, Brock University), but no US teacher-education adopter was independently confirmed this pass -- unlike Casper's separately-documented ~50-medical-school US footprint (peer's RULE-COUNSEL-120). Re-verify per-institution rather than assuming universally. Also confirms the peer session's RULE-COUNSEL-118 recommendation-vocabulary gap (no existing recommendation type for 'rehearse a timed situational-judgment response') is real in a second family, not hypothetical.
rules.note: Surfaced by following up on a cross-cutting lead the peer session flagged from its own medicine-family research (RULE-COUNSEL-120), not independently discovered by this session. Verified via direct fetch of Acuity Insights' own Teacher Education page plus 3 institutions' own admissions pages.

rules.statement: The Casper situational-judgment test (see RULE-COUNSEL-243 for the teaching instance) is also confirmed used for undergraduate engineering admissions -- Western University's Faculty of Engineering (Canada), starting Fall 2024, ~7,500 annual applicants. This is a fourth confirmed instance of the situational-judgment-test category (Queen's Commerce/McMaster response-scoring, Casper-teaching, UK UCAT/SJT-medicine, now Casper-engineering) and directly undergraduate-stage, unlike the business-education instance (RULE-COUNSEL-245). Confirmed adopter is Canadian; do not assume applicability to a US/UK-target engineering student without checking the specific program.
rules.note: Verified via direct fetch of Acuity Insights' own Western University press release, following up the same cross-cutting lead (RULE-COUNSEL-120/121) as RULE-COUNSEL-243.

rules.statement: Casper is marketed for business-education admissions, but the only specific adopter confirmed by direct fetch this pass -- Dalhousie University's Faculty of Management MBA program -- is graduate-level, not the undergraduate/high-school-applicant stage ORYN's population sits at. Do not present this as evidence that a current business-interested high schooler will encounter Casper; it establishes the assessment-category pattern generalizes here too, not that it is imminently relevant to this family's actual admissions stage.
rules.note: An honestly-scoped negative-ish finding, deliberately not forced into a parallel with RULE-COUNSEL-244's stronger (undergraduate-confirmed) engineering result.

rules.statement: Turkey's biomedical engineering sits under EMO (Elektrik Mühendisleri Odası, TMMOB's electrical-engineering chamber), confirmed via a dedicated named internal structure (Biyomedikal Mühendisligi Meslek Dali Ana Komisyonu) on EMO's own official page. Resolves this document's earlier 'genuinely unresolved' flag on whether biomedical engineering is treated separately or absorbed into an existing TMMOB chamber. Family 05's TMMOB/chamber-registration finding (RULE-COUNSEL-227) therefore applies to this family too, specifically through EMO.
